questions.q: What does consumerism promise but fail to deliver?
a: Lasting fulfillment from buying more things
Closer relationships with family and friends
A simpler and freer way of living
More control over your own time
questions.why: The first lesson says acquiring more only leads to wanting more, and the promised happy life never arrives.

questions.q: What does minimalism involve beyond decluttering your home?
a: Decluttering your mind and releasing toxic commitments
Buying only expensive, durable items
Living with almost no possessions at all
Avoiding social obligations whenever possible
questions.why: The second lesson says true minimalism also means letting go of bad relationships, toxic friendships and the lies we tell ourselves.

questions.q: Which of these is a foundational value, as the summary defines it?
a: Health and marriage
Hobbies and interests
Independence and kindness
A favorite television series
questions.why: Foundational values are the basic things that set the foundation for your life, such as health and marriage.

questions.q: What does the summary call ordinary things that only look important?
a: Imaginary values
Surface values
Structural values
Foundational values
questions.why: The third lesson describes imaginary values as things like a favorite Netflix show, which seem important but are not.

questions.q: What should you do before making an impulsive purchase?
a: Check whether the item aligns with your core values
Wait a month and see whether you still want it
Compare prices at several different stores
Ask a friend for their honest opinion
questions.why: The summary says to think through the four value categories before buying and drop the item if it only serves a surface or imaginary value.
